answer: Each identity is assigned one low-resource language seeded by its key and must pass a live monthly oral exam: two native examiners open a fresh conversation thread, drop in unseen prompts (describe a lagoon, bargain for a pearl) and score fluency against a recording hash posted beforehand. One operator cannot fake many tongues: 1,000 Sybils need 1,000 distinct fluent speakers, about 120 study hours and $600 tutoring each ($600,000), plus a 5-coin bond lost per failed or impersonated exam. Trade-off: admission is slow and tutors are scarce for rare languages.
